transcript: We have some great new features for our 2026.0 release. In Clo 2026.0 it is now possible to attach pattern pieces through gluing, in addition to sewing. There are three separate ways in which you can achieve this. The sticker approach, when you have internal shapes and patterns. Paintbrushes, when you have a specific area glued. And bucket glue, great for attaching a whole pattern on top of another. This update enhances production and accuracy of categories like athletic wear, outdoor wear, shoes and bags. Realizing ideas within Clo has never been easier or faster. Now you can truly sketch on an avatar and turn those sketches into patterns in an instant. Once you have your sketch, convert it into 3D pen lines to continue editing and adjust, or you can flatten the sketch and transform it into a pattern. It will then be arranged and sewn automatically. We have created an automatic lacing feature, so you can now quickly and easily lace shoes, bags and garments together. You can even create a lace pattern that could be edited or adjusted. Now, when you switch to the strain fit map, you will see a pop-up box that shows the options, global or fabric. When selecting global, parts of the garment where the strain is above 120% will highlight in red, no matter what type of fabric. Switching to fabric will customize the color range to match the fabric properties. We have added a few updates to our pattern draft. As always, you can quickly and easily add in your measurements by using a CSV file or typing in your numbers. You can also input grading information, simply add your graded size and then you can either add grading through rules or put in the graded measurements. Then you can create the pattern, which will automatically be arranged and sewn onto the avatar. Once created, the POM, or points of measure, will automatically be applied within the POM tab object browser with all the graded size information in case you added the grading. Then continue editing using the pattern drafter. As long as the pattern was created using the pattern drafter, you can enter the tool and edit the pattern. Or you can use the POM tool and edit the measurements directly within the 2D window. Our Calculator Notepad feature helps you create multiple calculations within your POM. Use the calculator icons and add the POMs into the calculator. Any basic arithmetic variations will work. From there, you can choose to apply it onto the notepad. If applied to the notepad, you can then see the calculation with the different grading, and also apply this new calculation into the POM object browser. You'll be able to see any calculations used in the POM. Within this update, you can lock custom measurements to the graphic or pattern outline. You can also create custom measurement points within the graphic and set the placement within the property editor. With Clou 2026.0, it's now easy to apply irregular grading quickly. Simply hold down Shift. Then click OK. And you can select multiple cells and change the measurement without affecting others. Under the setting button for nesting, you can now choose to bundle your pattern pieces for a single garment, making each garment have the same grain direction. This feature is useful when you have more than one grain direction. Clou 2026.0 will create a new Viewing option that will hide any non-selected part inside of the garment, making it easier to see inside of a garment, or view other angles that would otherwise be difficult to see and manipulate. We've improved Clou to allow viewing from your POM, along with the graphics, when using the schematic render. Not only will you use your POM tool when needed, but also when you review your POM during the assembly of your garment. This makes Clou 2026.0 easier to see if you want to see your garment in the pattern, or if you want to see the color and shape of your garment. render. Not only will you be able to see your points of measure, but you can choose which points of measure to view using the property editor POM tab, along with adjusting the sizing within the 3D inside the schematic render window. Now if you apply a graphic on fur, the graphic will automatically create a mask and cut away the fur so that you can properly see the graphic. There is also a way to customize the seam lines with fur, so you can control the fur thickness near a seam and determine how visible you want each seam to be through the Edit Sewing tool. Great news! In our efforts to improve the Closet user experience, the content page and workroom interface have been refreshed. The overview section of the Closet user experience is now available on the Closet 3D render window. The 3D render section will be shown when a 3D file is uploaded. From there, you can fill in the various fields, such as category. Users can also customize what's displayed on the first page by clicking the setting button in the right corner. Sub tabs will display additional information about the file, including version and linked content. We've also improved the 3D viewer on Closet. Now you can use the Closet quality render in the 3D live viewer. By clicking on the first option on the toggle bar, you can also access annotations and colorways by clicking on the tabs on the right hand corner. And by clicking the drop-down menu, versions can be managed. We've also refreshed the Bill of Materials section. By right-clicking each section in the BOM sheet, users can edit the data. It is possible to fill in a new BOM if it was not created in Closet. Next to BOM is the POM section. Similar to the BOM section, it shows the point of measure data according to the settings in Closet. In the attachment section, users can upload related documentation. There are also updates to comments and sharing. You can click the button on the right-hand corner to set permissions for sharing and commenting. And you can also review the activity log. You also have the option to switch the theme to dark mode for those of you that prefer it this way. And finally, at the workroom level, you can click the small eye button to preview the details of the garment quickly. We hope that these updates will improve collaboration for you and your teams using Closet, making it smoother, easier, and faster for all users. For more information, visit http://www.closet.com.au. For more information on additional new features and the latest updates on Clo 2026.0, check out our website at clo3d.com.
markdown_content: # Clo 2026.0 Release: Feature Highlights Clo 2026.0 introduces new ways to attach pattern pieces, sketch-to-pattern workflows, improved lacing and strain visualization, and expanded pattern drafting and editing tools. It also refreshes the Closet user experience across the content page and workroom interface. ## Attaching Pattern Pieces by Gluing (Sewing + Glue) This update adds the ability to attach pattern pieces through **gluing**, in addition to **sewing**. There are **three** distinct glue approaches for different use cases: 1. **Sticker approach** Use when you have **internal shapes and patterns** that need to be attached as a unit. 2. **Paintbrushes** Use when you have a **specific area** that should be glued. 3. **Bucket glue** Use to attach **a whole pattern on top of another**. These improvements enhance production and accuracy for categories such as **athletic wear, outdoor wear, shoes, and bags**, making it easier to realize design ideas faster. ## Sketch on Avatar → Pattern in Minutes (Sketch, 3D Pen Lines, Flatten) Clo 2026.0 streamlines the process of turning sketches into editable patterns. You can: - **Truly sketch on an avatar** - **Convert sketches into 3D pen lines** to continue editing and adjust in 3D - Or **flatten the sketch** and **transform it into a pattern** After conversion, Clo **arranges and sews automatically** onto the avatar. ## Automatic Lacing + Editable Lace Patterns Clo 2026.0 adds **automatic lacing**, allowing quick and easy lacing of: - **Shoes** - **Bags** - **Garments** You can also create a **lace pattern** that can be **edited or adjusted**, supporting iterative design without reworking the entire lacing setup. ## Strain Fit Map: Global vs Fabric Color Ranges When switching to the **strain fit map**, a **pop-up** appears with options for how strain is visualized: - **Global** Parts of the garment where strain is **above 120%** will **highlight in red**, regardless of fabric type. - **Fabric** The color range is **customized to match fabric properties**, providing more context-sensitive strain visualization. ## Pattern Drafting Updates: CSV Measurements, Grading, and Auto-Seam/Arrange Clo 2026.0 improves the **pattern draft** workflow with faster measurement input and grading support. ### Input measurements via CSV or direct entry You can add measurements by: - Importing a **CSV file**, or - **Typing** in your measurements. ### Grading information To grade: - Add your **graded size** - Then either: - Add grading **through rules**, or - Provide grading via **graded measurements** ### Pattern creation → auto arrangement and sewing on avatar When you create the pattern, Clo will **automatically arrange and sew** it onto the avatar. ### POM (Points of Measure) automation and editing - **POM is automatically applied** within the **POM tab** - In the **object browser**, POM includes **all graded size information** (if grading was added) - Continue editing using: - The **pattern drafter** tool (as long as the pattern was created using the pattern drafter), or - The **POM tool** to edit measurements directly within the **2D window** ## Calculator Notepad for POM Calculations (Arithmetic + Apply Back to POM) The **Calculator Notepad** feature helps you create multiple calculations tied to **POM** values. Workflow: - Use **calculator icons** - Add **POMs** into the calculator - Basic arithmetic variations work - Choose to **apply it onto the notepad** If applied: - You can see the calculation with **different grading** - You can apply the new calculation into the **POM object browser** - You can review any calculations used in the POM ## Lock Custom Measurements to Graphics/Outline + Custom Measurement Points This update adds measurement control options: - **Lock custom measurements** to the **graphic** or **pattern outline** - Create **custom measurement points** within the **graphic** - Set placement using the **property editor** ## Irregular Grading: Multi-Cell Edit with Shift + OK Clo 2026.0 enables faster irregular grading. Process: - **Hold down Shift** - **Click OK** - Select **multiple cells** and change measurements **without affecting others** ## Nesting Bundles: Same Garment Grain Direction In the settings for **nesting**, you can now **bundle pattern pieces for a single garment** so that each garment uses the **same grain direction**. This is useful when you have **more than one grain direction**. ## Viewing Improvements: Hide Non-Selected Parts + POM Viewing in Schematic Render ### Hide non-selected garment parts A new viewing option lets you **hide any non-selected part inside of the garment**, making it easier to see internal details and manipulate hard-to-reach areas. ### View from POM in schematic render Clo improves viewing so that you can view from the **POM**, not only from graphics, when using the **schematic render**. This also applies when reviewing your POM during garment assembly, helping you see: - The garment in the **pattern** - The **color and shape** of the garment You can: - View POM points - Choose which POM points to display using the **property editor (POM tab)** - Adjust sizing within the **3D** inside the **schematic render** window ## Graphics on Fur: Auto Mask + Cut Away + Seam Line Control When applying a **graphic on fur**, Clo will: - Automatically **create a mask** - **Cut away the fur** so the graphic is properly visible You can also customize seam appearance with fur: - Use the **Edit Sewing** tool to control **fur thickness near a seam** - Determine how visible each seam will be ## Closet Content Page + Workroom UI Refresh (Collaboration Improvements) Clo 2026.0 refreshes the **Closet** user experience to improve collaboration and workflow speed. ### Content page and workroom interface refresh - The **overview section** is now available on the **Closet 3D render window** - The **3D render section** appears when a **3D file is uploaded** - You can fill in fields such as **category** - Users can customize what appears on the first page via the **settings button** in the right corner - **Sub tabs** show additional file information, including **version** and **linked content** ### Improved 3D viewer in Closet - Use **Closet quality render** in the **3D live viewer** - Access **annotations** and **colorways** via tabs in the right-hand corner - Manage **versions** via the **drop-down menu** ### Bill of Materials (BOM) improvements - The **Bill of Materials** section is refreshed - Users can **right-click** sections in the **BOM sheet** to **edit data** - If BOM was not created in Closet, users can **fill in a new BOM** ### POM section in Closet - Next to BOM is the **POM** section - It shows **point of measure data** based on Clo/Closet settings ### Attachment, comments, sharing, and activity log - **Attachment**: upload related documentation - **Sharing and commenting** permissions via a button in the right-hand corner - **Activity log** can be reviewed ### Dark mode and quick garment preview - Optional **dark mode** - At workroom level, click the small **eye button** to preview garment details quickly ## References - http://www.closet.com.au - clo3d.com (additional new features and latest updates on Clo 2026.0)
